title: Vegetable Curry
subtitle: potato, cauliflower, spinach, and chickpeas in a spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: This is a simple, reliable vegetable curry that comes together in one pan. Potato and cauliflower give body, chickpeas add protein, and spinach wilts in at the end. The spice base is the kind of everyday blend used across northern India. Serve with rice or flatbread.
sourceNotes: Based on aloo gobi and chana masala traditions from northern Indian home cooking. The combination of potato, cauliflower, and chickpeas in a spiced tomato base is found across Punjab and neighbouring regions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Add spinach fresh when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. Good for batch cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Flavour improves the next day.

content.text: Fry the spices in hot oil before adding anything else. This blooms the spices and builds a much deeper flavour than adding them with the liquid.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add all the spices. Stir and fry for 1 minute.
Add the potato and cauliflower. Stir to coat in the spice base.
Add the tinned tomatoes and 200ml water. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes until the potato is tender. Add the chickpeas and cook for 5 more minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with rice or flatbread.

items.cause: Not enough liquid or cooked uncovered too long
items.fix: Add a splash of water and stir. Cover for the last 10 minutes.

items.symptom: Potato is still hard after 20 minutes
items.cause: Potato cut too large or heat too low
items.fix: Cut potato into smaller pieces next time. Cover and raise the heat slightly.

content.text: This curry draws on the everyday home cooking of northern India, where combinations of potato, cauliflower, and chickpeas in spiced tomato sauce are staples. Dishes like aloo gobi and chana masala have been made for generations. This recipe merges the two traditions into a single weeknight dish that is reliably satisfying.
